title: compute/v1 Computer
description: The one unit of the compute layer: a machine reachable by SSH. kind device = a computer or server where the person installed the client (AgentDevice); kind sandbox = a cloud sandbox this layer created on demand (POST /v1/sandboxes), running the same client. Facts are reported as they are; differences between systems are not smoothed over (the Agent knows them). README.md: contracts/compute/v1/README.md.

name.description: The person's name for a device (「台式机」); for a sandbox the name its creator gave (POST /v1/sandboxes `name`).

own.description: The owner (identity/v1 `own`): the computer is in this owner's network and only tokens with this `own` reach it.

state.description: From the connection layer (the NetBird peer's status; for a sandbox also its provider's lifecycle), never stored as a second copy. online: its client is connected and SSH answers. offline: it should be reachable and is not (device switched off, network lost), or a sandbox whose create failed (`sandbox.failure` says why; it never comes online). sleeping: a stopped sandbox (:start wakes it). starting: a sandbox being created or started, or a device whose client is connecting.

version.description: The AgentDevice client version running on it.

sandbox.description: Present exactly when kind is sandbox.

facts.description: What the machine is, reported by its client (PUT /v1/computers/{id}/facts) and refreshed when it changes. Every value is what the system says; nothing is mapped to a common vocabulary beyond the enums below.

name.description: As the system names itself ("Windows 11 Pro", "Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS", "macOS 15.6").

arch.description: Go GOARCH naming, as the client (Go) reports it: amd64, arm64, 386, arm, riscv64, …

shell.description: The shell an SSH session of `user` (POST /v1/computers/{id}/access) runs commands in.

name.description: bash, zsh, fish, sh, pwsh, powershell, cmd, …

cores.description: Logical cores; a sandbox reports its vCPU limit (may be fractional).

software.description: Programs found on the PATH of `user` that the client looks for (toolchains, package managers, editors, runtimes), each as found.

specDigest.description: Digest of the spec it was created with (canonical JSON), for caching and comparison.

holds.description: Live holds (a lapsed hold is dropped). A sandbox without one is reclaimed at `reclaimAt`, except a long one never held.

reclaimAt.description: Present when nothing keeps the sandbox: when it is removed (its last hold ended + 30 minutes for temporary, + 6 hours for long; a failed sandbox 30 minutes after it failed, whatever holds it).

network.description: Present when the sandbox has an allow list (README "Egress"); absent: every public host.

stopping.description: Present while the sandbox's node is drained for a restart (2026-11-06, additive, AgentCompute#89; the same as its computer.stopping event): the sandbox stops at `deadline` at the latest. Hand the work over and release the hold before then.

failure.description: Present when the sandbox's create failed (2026-11-08, additive, AgentCompute#163): it never runs, `state` stays offline, every call that needs it (access, holds, :start, :stop) is refused with COMPUTE_SANDBOX_FAILED carrying this as its cause, and it is removed 30 minutes after `at` whatever holds it. The problem's facts (R22): which part failed, during what, the cause chain as it came (e.g. the node's Docker/Sysbox error), and what to do: create a new sandbox (a new Idempotency-Key).

retryable.description: false: this sandbox will not come up; a new one may.

cause.description: The cause chain, as it came: { code?, component?, status?, detail, cause? }.
